title: I finished my game in just 4 days using vibe coding, and the demo is now live on Steam now
author: AlfishGames
selftext:
I’ve been developing games for 9 years, mostly working on hyper casual mobile games. Now, I’m excited to share my first Steam game, created with the help of AI.

Trying the demo and adding the game to your wishlist would mean a lot and would greatly support the project.

If you’re curious about which AI tools I used or how I approached the development process, I’d be happy to share the details.

Steam Link: [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4920710/Keep_On_Nailing)

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: is it gonna get less derivative over time? When you release a demo that should mean that's the game that you're going to be releasing - but more of it.

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
Honestly, yes, there are a lot of games in this style, but I don’t think it’s fair to call every game after the first one a copy.

So far, it seems like the game is successfully delivering the kind of feeling that players who enjoy this genre are looking for.

For the Early Access version, I’m planning to add more skills, a hammer crafting system, new maps, and upgrade nodes that make each session feel different while still keeping the experience cozy.

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: Cool, good luck!

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body: Thank you!

replies.author: holdmyspot123
replies.body: You don't need to fix it being similar to other games; you are clearly learning.  No need to be defensive

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body: Thanks for your comment. What I was really trying to say is that being similar to other games isn’t necessarily a bad thing. I completely agree with you, and thanks again!

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
Taking inspiration from other games is a perfectly valid way to develop a game idea. That said, I couldn’t find another game with the same visual style or core concept as this one.

I think it feels good to play and that the gameplay works well. It currently has 316 players with a median playtime of 42 minutes, which doesn’t seem too bad.

Is the fact that I made it in four days what bothers you, or is there something else? I’m happy to discuss any part of it in as much detail as you’d like.

replies.author: Aware-Source6313
replies.body: Because that is literally far and away where AI tools have the most leverage and value add -- rehashing existing ideas with an obvious template at BLAZING speeds. If you don't need originality it can make the decisions and do the thinking for you. This is the maximum ratio of output:effort.

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
I never told the AI to simply recreate another game. Of course I had references, and honestly, I think everyone should have references when making a game.

What I wanted to prove, both to myself and to others, was that if you define a scope that AI can realistically handle, it’s possible to build something at this speed and still reach a solid level of quality.

Also, let’s not ignore the fact that the median playtime is currently 42 minutes. That probably means people are enjoying the game, right?

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
Thank you! The visuals were generated with Nano Banana 2, and I used Claude for the coding.

In my experience, Claude works really well with Godot. I also tried building the same project in Unity, but I honestly think Godot is a much better fit for vibe coding.

I believe you can get good results with other AI tools and game engines too, as long as you clearly explain what you want, make precise adjustments during the polishing stage, and have at least some technical knowledge.

comments.author: bonsoir-world
comments.body:
Could you share what you used AI wise and how you managed to make it? 

Just getting into AI and game dev potential. I see some people using purely ‘AI Game’ platforms and so using multiple platform’s, to generate assets, do other workflows and then connecting Claude or the likes to an engine MCP. 

Hard to nail down (no pun intended) a decent process, especially as a newbie with some ideas. 

Cool game by the way!

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
Thank you! I answered some of this in my previous comment, but I’m happy to share a bit more detail.

I prepared the game’s GDD with ChatGPT. Then I quickly built the first prototype in Claude Design, exported it as a .zip file, and gave it to Claude with instructions to recreate the prototype in Godot.

The most important thing during development was working step by step. Even with AI, it’s not realistic to ask for everything at once and expect a polished result. I first polished the main scene, then focused on the impact and feel of each hit, then the nails, and continued improving each part separately until the game reached its current state.

For the visuals, I had Claude write prompts for Nano Banana 2. Whenever the generated images didn’t match the art style or quality I wanted, I asked ChatGPT to create a concept image, then used that reference to explain my vision to Claude more clearly and generate new visuals.

That’s probably the shortest detailed summary I can give of the process.

replies.author: FI5HYVR
replies.body: How thorough were the directions in Claude design? Full fidelity vs wireframes, just a few screens or complete product, and static or interactive?

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body:
On the Claude Design side, I didn’t spend any time worrying about the visuals or trying to polish them. My main focus was making sure the mechanics and core gameplay loop worked properly.

I added all the essential details of the main mechanic in Claude Design so I would have a solid foundation I could build on and improve later. Once that was ready, I moved the project into Godot and started developing the game on top of that base.

replies.author: bonsoir-world
replies.body:
Amazing, thank you! 

Wishing you success with your game. I think AI can unlock so much creativity, even if its for working prototypes before ‘proper development’.

replies.author: AlfishGames
replies.body: Thank you so much. I completely agree with you. I’ve developed many games manually before, and applying the same pipeline while using AI gave me really good results
